title: Client hunks depend on shared symbols that this diff never defines — codec (AC5) and attempt_log payload are unshipped here
evidence:
+  ReferenceAwaitingCorrection, ReferenceCompleted, ReferenceDeclined,
+  ReferenceObjected, ReferenceUnreachable, VacancyClosed, VacancyClosing,
+  VacancyExtended,

+  type AttemptLogEntry, type ReferenceCallAttempt, type ReferenceCallDetail,

- **EDIT:** `shared/src/shared/notification.gleam` (5 variants + arms) ·
  `shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam` (AttemptLogEntry + `attempt_log`
  key, back-compat decoder) ·
detail: Client code imports five reference_* variants, AttemptLogEntry, and a ReferenceCallDetail.attempt_log field, but no shared/ or server/ hunks define them — the spec's own Files list those edits as part of this change. Without them the client cannot compile and AC5 is unshipped.
recommended_fix: Include the shared/notification.gleam codec (5 variants + arms), reference_call.gleam AttemptLogEntry/attempt_log decoder, and the server builder/stamp changes in this changeset, or explicitly split this diff.

title: collapse_same_at_sends drops any consecutive same-at line, including lifecycle lines — contradicts its own doc comment
detail: The guard compares only `at`, not kind: a form_opened/corrected/taken_over/terminal entry sharing its exact timestamp with the previous line is silently dropped from both the rendered timeline and the export, despite the comment promising lifecycle lines pass through untouched.
recommended_fix: Restrict the collapse to send kinds (e.g. require prev.kind and line.kind both in invitation_sent/co_nudge/reminder_sent before deduping), or key the dedupe on (at, kind).

title: Terminal label and export-outcome tables omit Completed and Failed — fallbacks misstate finished rows
evidence:
+  type ReferenceCallStatus, AwaitingCorrection, Calling, CharacterRef, Completed,
+  ContactInitiated, EmployerRef, Failed, FormCompleted, LandlordRef,

+    "form_completed" -> "Reference received"
+    "manual_recorded" -> "Recorded manually"
+    "partial" -> "Form left unfinished"
+    _ -> "In progress"

+    "partial" -> "Form left unfinished"
+    _ -> "Closed"
detail: Completed and Failed are terminal statuses the panel renders (view_completed handles Completed; Failed has state copy), yet neither new case table has arms for them. A terminal Failed row exports Outcome "In progress" — factually wrong for an evidence-grade record.
recommended_fix: Add explicit arms for "completed" and "failed" (and audit scheduled/calling) to refcheck_timeline_terminal and refcheck_export_outcome so terminal rows never fall through to generic labels.

title: Legacy payloads without attempt_log render an empty expanded ContactInitiated row — attempt summary deleted with no fallback
evidence:
+  let attempt_log = case call.status, list.is_empty(call.attempt_log) {
+    Queued, _ -> element.none()
+    Skipped, _ -> element.none()
+    _, True -> element.none()
+    _, False -> view_attempt_log(call, slot)
+  }

     ContactInitiated ->
-      html.div([class("space-y-3")], [
-        view_attempt_summary(call),
-        case
detail: The old ContactInitiated body (view_attempt_summary built from the still-shipped attempts key) is deleted; with attempt_log defaulting to [] for pre-deploy payloads, an in-flight row with no pending takeover confirm now expands to nothing — send history and next-steps hint lost during the rollout window.
recommended_fix: Fall back to rendering the attempts-derived summary when attempt_log is empty, or keep view_attempt_summary for ContactInitiated until the server payload with attempt_log is guaranteed in production.

title: New runtime label "Closed — no reply" carries an em-dash without the explicit spec-verbatim exclusion the toast got
detail: The dash-free rule for implementer-authored strings is restated in the spec, and only the OQ-5 toast receives a documented verbatim exclusion. This function's em-dash string got neither, and as a fn result it evades the const-list scan regardless.
recommended_fix: If "Closed — no reply" is genuinely §7.6 verbatim, document the spec-verbatim exclusion beside the fn; otherwise rephrase dash-free (e.g. "Closed with no reply").

title: Dropdown test constructs Notification records directly — never exercises the codec decode path AC5 exists to protect
evidence:
+    let notif =
+      notification.Notification(
+        id: "n-ref",

+    html |> string.contains("Reference event") |> should.be_true
detail: AC5's failure mode is the shared decoder rejecting one unknown reference_* type and failing the whole list decode — but this test builds values directly and asserts only the title, and all five types share one icon arm, so neither decode nor per-type rendering is pinned.
recommended_fix: Add a shared-level test that decodes a JSON notifications list containing all five reference_* types, and assert the dropdown renders a decoded notification rather than a constructed one.
